 Key Points Transcript codes are three-digit IRS transaction codes on your account transcript. Code 846 with a date means the IRS issued your refund, and code 570 means something is holding it.
 Where’s My Refund reference codes are four-digit codes from the IRS refund tracker. The IRS manual updated in September 2026 lists 38 of them, and several mean a letter is on the way.
 Paper refund checks are no longer the default. A return filed without bank information gets its refund frozen and a CP53E notice, with 30 days to add an account online.
 Your IRS tax transcript and the Where’s My Refund tracker both use codes, and they don’t mean the same thing. Transcript codes are three-digit transaction codes, such as 150, 570 and 846. Reference codes are four-digit numbers that appear in the refund tracker, such as 1121 or 9001.
 This page lists every transaction code the IRS publishes for account transcripts and every reference code in the current IRS manual. It also shows which code combinations mean a refund is on the way. If you’d rather skip the codes, our IRS tax refund calendar shows typical deposit timing by filing date.
 We update this list before every filing season, and this version is built for returns filed in 2027. The questions readers ask most are collected in our list of Where’s My Refund questions and errors .

 How Do You Look Up An IRS Code?
 Type the code into the lookup below to see what it means and what to do next. It searches the three-digit transcript codes and the four-digit Where’s My Refund codes on this page. An eight-digit number next to a transaction is a cycle code, and our IRS cycle codes breakdown shows how to read it.
 IRS Code Lookup Enter a transcript code or Where’s My Refund reference code Look Up 846 570 971 290 898 1121 1242 9001 Searches every code table on this page. Source: IRS. The College Investor. 
 What Is An IRS Account Transcript?
 An IRS account transcript is a record of everything posted to your tax account for one tax year. It shows the return posting, your credits, payments, holds, offsets and the refund, each with a transaction code and a date. It’s one of five transcript types, and our tax transcripts overview covers the other four.
 The fastest way to get it is your IRS online account, where the IRS Get Transcript page lets you view, print or download it. You can also order a mailed copy at 800-908-9946, and it arrives in five to 10 calendar days. If identity verification fails online, you may need to contact the IRS or use the mail option.
 The new IRS app replaced IRS2Go on September 25, 2026, and signing in gives you access to your tax records on your phone. Form 4506-T still works for mailed copies of any transcript type, which helps if a lender or the FAFSA needs a different transcript .
 How Do You Read An IRS Account Transcript?
 Start with the transactions section at the bottom of the account transcript. Each line shows a code, a short explanation, a cycle number, a date and an amount. The cycle number tells you when the IRS posted the entry, as our cycle code breakdown explains.
 Example IRS account transcript with transaction codes 
 Read the transactions in this order:
 Find TC 150. Your return has posted, and the amount next to it is the tax assessed.
 Check the credits. TC 806 is your withholding, TC 766 is a refundable credit and TC 768 is the earned income credit.
 Look for holds. TC 570, TC 810 and TC 971 are the entries that slow a refund down.
 Find TC 846. The date next to it is the date the IRS issued your refund.
 Watch for offsets. TC 898 means a Treasury offset took some of the refund, and TC 826 means the IRS moved it to a balance in another year.
 A TC 898 offset pays a debt such as past-due child support, a state tax bill or another federal debt, according to the IRS refunds page . Defaulted federal student loans are one of those debts, and our breakdown of whether student loans will take your tax refund covers where collections stand.
 Which Transcript Codes Matter Most For Your Refund?
 Code 846 is the one most filers wait for, since it means the IRS issued the refund. Codes 570, 810 and 971 are the ones that mean your return needs a closer look. The table below covers the codes that show up on most refund returns, drawn from IRS Document 6209 . Codes tied to the earned income tax credit carry an extra wait because of the PATH Act.
 IRS Transcript Codes That Matter For Your Refund Code What It Means What To Do 
 150 Your return posted and the tax on it was assessed Nothing. This is the first step for every return. 
 806 Federal income tax withheld, from your W-2s and 1099s Nothing, as long as it matches your forms. 
 766 A refundable credit posted, such as the additional child tax credit Nothing, unless the amount differs from your return. 
 768 The earned income credit posted Expect the PATH Act hold, so no refund before February 15. 
 570 A hold on the refund for a pending liability or review Watch for TC 971 and a letter. TC 571 lifts the hold. 
 571 The TC 570 hold was released Look for TC 846 next. 
 810 Refund freeze Wait for a letter. TC 811 lifts the freeze. 
 971 A miscellaneous action, such as a notice being issued Check your mail and your IRS online account. 
 290 Additional tax assessed. A $0.00 amount can release an earlier hold Look for TC 846 or a notice. 
 846 Refund issued, with the refund date next to it Expect the deposit around that date. 
 898 The Treasury Offset Program took some or all of the refund for a debt Call the Bureau of the Fiscal Service at 800-304-3107. 
 420 / 424 Return referred for examination Wait for the IRS letter before you respond. 
 977 An amended return posted to your account Track it in Where’s My Amended Return. 
 Source: IRS Document 6209 and Internal Revenue Manual 21.4.1. The College Investor. 
 A TC 570 followed by a TC 971 means the IRS sent a notice. On a refund return, that notice can be a CP05 letter saying the IRS is verifying your income, withholding or credits. Answer any request by its deadline, because the refund stays on hold until the review closes.
 What Do Common Transcript Code Combinations Mean?
 Single codes rarely tell the whole story, and the order they post in matters more. These are the combinations that show up on refund returns and what each one means for your money. The newer entries tied to direct deposit come from the Internal Revenue Manual section IRS phone staff use for refund questions. The IRS sent about 4 million notices for missing or wrong bank information by April 27, 2026, according to the National Taxpayer Advocate . Those rows explain many of the refund delays readers will see in 2027.
 Common IRS Transcript Code Combinations Codes You See What It Means What Happens Next 
 150, 806, 846 The return processed and the refund was issued The deposit arrives around the 846 date. 
 150, 768 Or 766, 846 Earned income credit or additional child tax credit refund, held by the PATH Act The 846 date can’t fall before February 15. 
 570, Then 971 The refund is on hold and the IRS sent a notice Read the notice and answer by its deadline. 
 570, 971, Then 571 The hold was placed and then released TC 846 follows if nothing else is owed. 
 570, Then 290 For $0.00 A review closed without changing your tax Look for TC 846. 
 971 AC 804, No 846 The refund is frozen for missing or rejected bank information (CP53E) Add a bank account in your IRS online account within 30 days. 
 970 AC 001, Then 846 You added a bank account online TC 846 posts within one to two weeks. 
 971 AC 850, Then 846 A paper check waiver was approved, or the bank account couldn’t be verified The check arrives within four weeks of the 846 date. 
 841, No New 846 The bank returned your direct deposit Watch for a CP53E notice. 
 846, Then 898 A Treasury offset reduced the refund The Bureau of the Fiscal Service mails an offset notice. 
 826 And 706 The refund was applied to a balance in another tax year Check that year’s transcript. 
 971 AC 696 The Bureau of the Fiscal Service confirmed it received the refund record Nothing. It doesn’t mean an offset. 
 Source: IRS Document 6209 and Internal Revenue Manual 21.4.1. The College Investor. 
 A TC 898 on a joint return can take your share of the refund for your spouse’s debt. In that case, Form 8379 injured spouse relief is how you ask for your portion back.
 What’s Changing For The 2027 Tax Season?
 The biggest change is that paper refund checks are no longer the default. The IRS began phasing out paper refund checks on September 30, 2025, under Executive Order 14247. The 2027 filing season will be the second one under those rules. If you don’t have a bank account, our list of second-chance checking accounts covers options for people who’ve been turned down before.
 The shift happened fast. Paper check refunds fell to 2.2 million from January 1 through May 26, 2026, according to the National Taxpayer Advocate . That’s down from 8.4 million in the same stretch of 2025. About 98% of refunds went out by direct deposit, which is why a free checking account is the simplest way to avoid a delay.
 What Happens If You File Without Direct Deposit Information?
 The IRS still processes the return, but it freezes the refund. You’ll get a CP53E notice giving you 30 days to add a bank account in your IRS online account or pick a paper check exception. That same notice goes out when your bank rejects a deposit, which is a common reason a refund seems to vanish after the expected deposit date .
 If you do nothing, the freeze releases after six weeks and the IRS mails a paper check. The CP53E is only issued once, so a second rejected deposit goes straight to a paper check. Our walkthrough on how to cash a tax refund check without a bank account helps if that’s where you land.
 Paper check exceptions cover nine situations, including a disability, no access to a bank, an ITIN, an international bank account and incarceration. Once the IRS approves an exception, TC 971 AC 850 posts and the check arrives within four weeks of the TC 846 date. A plan for your tax refund helps if a slower check throws off your budget. These are the entries the IRS refund manual ties to the new rules, and your own transcript may show them with a shorter description.
 New Direct Deposit Entries For The 2027 Tax Season Code What It Means 
 TC 971 AC 804 CP53E notice issued for a frozen or rejected direct deposit refund 
 TC 970 AC 001 Bank account added through your IRS online account 
 TC 971 AC 850 Refund switched to a paper check after a waiver or a failed bank check 
 TC 841 Direct deposit returned by the bank, with a P- freeze on the refund 
 TC 846 Refund issued, once the bank account or waiver is in place 
 Source: Internal Revenue Manual 21.4.1, updated September 2026. The College Investor. 
 When Does The 2027 Tax Season Start?
 The IRS hasn’t announced the 2027 opening day yet. The 2026 season opened January 26, 2026, and the IRS announced that date on January 8. We’ll update our page on when IRS e-file opens as soon as the 2027 date is set.
 Returns for tax year 2026 are due April 15, 2027, as listed on our tax due dates page. By law, refunds on returns that claim the earned income tax credit or the additional child tax credit can’t be issued before February 15. Our PATH Act refund dates page tracks when those refunds actually land.
 What Else Changed Since Last Tax Season?
 Three smaller changes affect what you see in the refund tracker and on your transcript. Each one explains a code or screen that confused readers in past seasons, and our list of reasons your tax return could be delayed covers the rest.
 The IRS app replaced IRS2Go. Refund status still works without signing in, according to the IRS app FAQ .
 Savings bonds are gone from refunds. TreasuryDirect ended paper savings bond purchases with tax refunds on January 1, 2025, so WMR codes 2015 to 2017 only apply to older returns.
 Tax Topic 152 now points to the IRS refunds page. The old “Refer to Tax Topic 152” message in the tracker sends you to the IRS refunds page , which lists typical refund timing.
 Review volume is the other thing to plan for. The Taxpayer Advocate’s June 2026 report found more than 14 million individual returns were suspended during processing in the 2026 season. More than one million taxpayers waited past normal processing times. Filing an accurate return with a valid bank account is still the best protection, and our ranking of the best tax software covers tools that catch errors before you file.
 Full List Of IRS Transaction Codes
 The table below lists 382 transaction codes from Document 6209 , the IRS manual of processing codes. Many apply only to business, employment or estate accounts, so an individual filer will see a small set of them. If a code shows a penalty or balance you can’t pay, an IRS payment plan keeps it from growing into collections.
 The most recent public edition of Section 8A is dated 2023, and every code here appears in it. The table scrolls, and the lookup at the top of this page jumps straight to any row. For a full overview of how refunds move, see our refund schedule .

 What Are Where’s My Refund Reference Codes?
 Reference codes are four-digit codes that Where’s My Refund and the IRS app show when a refund is delayed or changed. They come from Exhibit 21.4.1-3 of the Internal Revenue Manual, which IRS phone staff use to explain refund status. Reference code 9001 has its own page, covering what IRS reference number 9001 means .
 The IRS updated that manual section on September 2, 2026, and it now lists 38 codes. Codes in the 1000s cover holds, offsets and reviews, while the 2000s cover returned checks and savings bonds. The 5500s cover split deposits, and the 9000s cover system issues and math errors .
 Where’s My Refund Reference Codes For 2027 Code What It Means What To Do 
 1001 Paper refund check mailed more than four weeks ago Request a refund trace if the check hasn’t arrived. 
 1021 The Bureau of the Fiscal Service took part of the refund for a debt, and a check was mailed more than four weeks ago Call the Treasury Offset Program at 800-304-3107. 
 1081 The IRS applied all or part of the refund to a tax debt, and a check was mailed more than four weeks ago Look for the IRS notice that explains the offset. 
 1091 The IRS applied all or part of the refund to a tax debt, and a direct deposit went out more than a week ago Look for the IRS notice that explains the offset. 
 1121 A problem was found on the account, with a P- freeze Check your IRS online account for a CP53E or other notice. 
 1141 Refund delayed by a liability on another account, with a V- freeze Expect a notice about the other balance. 
 1161 Refund delayed by a bankruptcy on the account, for less than eight weeks Ask your bankruptcy attorney or trustee. 
 1181 Refund pulled for review, outside seven processing cycles Wait for an IRS letter. 
 1221 Refund pulled for review, within seven processing cycles Wait for an IRS letter. 
 1241 Paper return received more than six weeks ago and in review (E- freeze), with a notice coming Answer the notice by its deadline. 
 1242 E-filed return received more than three weeks ago and in review (E- freeze), with a notice coming Answer the notice by its deadline.

 What Should You Do If You See A Reference Code?
 Match the code to the table above, then check whether it asks you to do anything. Many reference codes only mean a letter is coming. Calling early won’t help, since the IRS refund manual tells phone staff not to research a refund before normal processing time has passed. That window is three weeks for an e-filed return and six weeks for a mailed one, so mark the date before you call the IRS .
 Check your mail and your IRS online account. Most holds come with a notice, and a CP53E shows up online before it arrives by mail.
 Call about offsets in the right place. For codes 1021, 1341 to 1401 and 5501, the Treasury Offset Program line at 800-304-3107 tells you which agency took the money.
 Call the IRS once the window passes. The main line is 800-829-1040, and the automated refund line is 800-829-1954.
 Ask for help if the delay causes a hardship. The Taxpayer Advocate Service takes cases where a delay is causing financial harm.
 If a student loan offset took your refund, our steps for stopping tax offsets for student loan debt explain how to get out of default before next year.
 How Is Where’s My Refund Different From Your Transcript?
 Where’s My Refund shows a simple status, while the account transcript shows every action behind it. Use the tracker for a quick timing check and the transcript when you need to see why a refund is held or reduced. Both pull from your IRS account, so a TC 846 on the transcript and a “Refund Sent” status describe the same event on our refund calendar .

 Frequently Asked Questions
 What Does Code 846 Mean On An IRS Transcript?
 TC 846 means the IRS issued your refund, and the date next to it is the refund date. A direct deposit lands around that date, while a paper check takes longer to arrive. Our refund calendar shows typical timing. If a TC 898 follows the 846, an offset reduced the amount.
 What Does Code 570 Mean On An IRS Transcript?
 TC 570 puts a hold on your refund while the IRS reviews something or checks for another liability. A TC 571 releases the hold, and a TC 290 for $0.00 can also clear it. If a TC 971 posts after the 570, look for a notice such as a CP05 letter .
 What Does Code 971 Mean On An IRS Transcript?
 TC 971 is a miscellaneous transaction, and the action code after it says what happened. On a refund return, it can mark a notice being issued. TC 971 AC 804 means a CP53E notice for missing bank information, and TC 971 AC 696 only means the Bureau of the Fiscal Service received the refund record.
 What Does IRS Reference Code 1121 Mean?
 Reference code 1121 means the IRS found a problem on the account and placed a P- freeze on the refund. Under the 2026 direct deposit rules, a deposit rejected by your bank also posts with a P- freeze. Check your IRS online account for a CP53E notice before you contact the IRS .
 What Is Code 599 On An IRS Transcript?
 TC 599 is a satisfying transaction that closes a non-filing case because the IRS secured your return. It shows up when the IRS had flagged a year as unfiled and then received the return. It doesn’t signal a refund problem, and our steps for late filing taxes cover what to do if you still owe.
 What Are MFT Codes On An IRS Transcript?
 MFT stands for master file tax account code, and it identifies the type of tax on a transcript. MFT 30 covers most Form 1040 individual income tax returns. Other MFT codes apply to business, employment and penalty accounts.
 Is A Transcript Request The Same As Checking Where’s My Refund?
 No. Where’s My Refund only shows refund status, while a transcript is an official record of your account. You request transcripts online, by phone at 800-908-9946 or with Form 4506-T by mail.
